findings.title: Hardcoded Test Signature Bypass in Razorpay Webhook Ingress
findings.observation: router.ts:1174 contains the conditional check: 'if (signature !== "mock_signature" && !webhookProcessor.verifySignature(rawBody, signature))'. Supplying the exact string 'mock_signature' in the 'x-razorpay-signature' header bypasses HMAC SHA-256 verification unconditionally.
findings.attack_reproduction: Send an HTTP POST to /webhooks/razorpay with header 'x-razorpay-signature: mock_signature' and payload '{ "event": "payment.captured", "payload": { "order": { "entity": { "id": "<target_order_id>" } } } }'. The request is accepted with HTTP 200 without cryptographic verification.
findings.expected: HMAC SHA-256 signature verification must be enforced unconditionally on every incoming webhook payload.
findings.actual: Header 'x-razorpay-signature: mock_signature' bypasses cryptographic signature verification completely.
findings.impact: Remote unauthorized financial settlement manipulation: An external attacker can fake payment captures, commit reservations, and trigger fulfillment dispatches without paying.
findings.evidence: Source inspection of src/gateway/router.ts:1174 and live pentest execution confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'signature !== "mock_signature"' from production routing code. In automated tests, generate valid HMAC SHA-256 signatures using the test webhook secret instead of bypassing verification.
findings.regression_test_required: Assert that 'POST /webhooks/razorpay' with 'x-razorpay-signature: mock_signature' returns HTTP 401 INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Direct Dual-Resource Reservation Creation via POST /v1/reservations
findings.observation: Route POST /v1/reservations exposes direct access to reservationEngine.holdReservation() without any Fastify preHandler scope check (requireScope) and without evaluating Ed25519 mandate signatures, revocation status, or merchant policy.
findings.attack_reproduction: Issue an anonymous HTTP POST to /v1/reservations with body: { intent_id: '<uuid>', mandate: { mandate_id: 'forged_mandate', budget_limit: 1000000 }, items: [{ sku: 'SKU-KEYBOARD-RGB', quantity: 5 }] }. The server responds HTTP 201 Created and decrements real merchant catalog stock.
findings.expected: Direct reservation endpoints must require administrative authorization (merchant:policy:write) or enforce full 6-phase mandate signature verification.
findings.actual: Locks real catalog inventory units anonymously without authentication or signature verification.
findings.impact: Denial of Inventory / Resource Exhaustion: An unauthenticated malicious actor can lock up all merchant inventory in 'HELD' reservations anonymously, causing denial of service to legitimate buyers.
findings.evidence: Source code in router.ts:1684-1701 and verified absence of requireScope preHandler.
findings.recommendation: Add '{ preHandler: [requireScope("merchant:policy:write")] }' or remove the public route if not required for external control plane integration.
findings.regression_test_required: Assert that unauthenticated POST /v1/reservations returns HTTP 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

findings.title: Runtime Bypass of Formal Payment State Machine in Webhook Handler
findings.observation: FinancialStateMachine is defined in src/core/state_machine.ts and imported in src/gateway/router.ts:19, but FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition() is NEVER invoked in router.ts or webhook.ts before mutating order_sessions.status.
findings.attack_reproduction: Submit a payment.captured webhook with a new event ID for an order session that is currently in 'REFUNDED' or 'PAYMENT_FAILED'. webhook.ts:117 blindly executes UPDATE order_sessions SET status = 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED' and calls triggerFulfillment() regardless of previous status.
findings.expected: Every state mutation must invoke FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition(currentStatus, targetStatus) and reject illegal transitions (e.g. REFUNDED -> CAPTURED, PAYMENT_FAILED -> CAPTURED).
findings.actual: State is overwritten via raw SQL UPDATE statement without validating against the formal transition map.
findings.impact: Out-of-order or duplicate webhook events can resurrect terminated or refunded orders, causing double fulfillment or inconsistent financial states.
findings.evidence: Grep search confirming FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition is only called in unit tests, not in runtime order update paths.
findings.recommendation: Integrate FinancialStateMachine.validateTransition(orderSession.status, 'CAPTURED') inside RazorpayWebhookProcessor.processEvent before executing SQL updates.
findings.regression_test_required: Send payment.captured webhook for an order with status 'REFUNDED'; assert transition is rejected as illegal financial state transition.

findings.title: HMAC Verification Computed over Re-Serialized JSON Body Instead of Raw Buffer
findings.observation: router.ts:1169 executes 'const rawBody = JSON.stringify(request.body);' and passes rawBody to verifySignature. Fastify parses the request stream into an object first; re-stringification does not guarantee identical whitespace, key ordering, or byte representation as Razorpay's wire transmission.
findings.attack_reproduction: Send a valid Razorpay webhook with spaces or non-standard key ordering. The HMAC computed over JSON.stringify(request.body) differs from the signature generated by Razorpay over original wire bytes.
findings.expected: Webhook HMAC signature must be verified against the exact, unparsed incoming raw byte Buffer.
findings.actual: Verification uses re-serialized JSON string from parsed object.
findings.impact: Production integration instability: Legitimate payment notifications from Razorpay may fail verification and be rejected with 401 INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE, leaving orders uncaptured.
findings.evidence: Source code in router.ts:1169 ('const rawBody = JSON.stringify(request.body);').
findings.recommendation: Enable Fastify raw body preservation (e.g. fastify-raw-body plugin) and pass request.rawBody Buffer directly to crypto.createHmac().
findings.regression_test_required: Verify webhook signature verification passes when payload contains non-standard JSON formatting (extra spaces, newlines).

findings.title: Static Plaintext Administrative Bearer Tokens Embedded in Source Code
findings.observation: Static administrative bearer tokens ('secret_merchant_admin', 'secret_merchant_viewer', 'secret_audit_bot') are defined in a hardcoded dictionary in source code.
findings.attack_reproduction: Inspect src/gateway/auth.ts, extract 'secret_merchant_admin', and pass 'Authorization: Bearer secret_merchant_admin' to PUT /v1/merchant/policy or POST /v1/mandates/revoke.
findings.expected: Administrative credentials must be loaded from secure environment variables or verified via asymmetric signed JWTs with short expirations.
findings.actual: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in source code provide permanent full administrative privileges.
findings.impact: Credential exposure: Anyone with read access to the repository or Docker image has administrative control over merchant policies, mandate revocations, and audit logs.
findings.recommendation: Migrate administrative authentication to environment-configured API keys (e.g. process.env.ACG_ADMIN_TOKEN) or asymmetric JWTs.
findings.regression_test_required: Ensure hardcoded fallback tokens are strictly rejected in production mode.

findings.title: Hardcoded Latency and Status Telemetry in Gateway API Responses
findings.observation: Endpoints /dashboard/metrics and /dashboard/health return static literal values for several performance and status indicators: measured_cold_run_ms: 286.3, is_sandbox_connected: true, latency_ms: 12, mode: 'Sandbox', and payment_intelligence.model: 'vulcan-v1.4-live-transformer'.
findings.attack_reproduction: Query GET /dashboard/metrics and GET /dashboard/health. The latency is always exactly 286.3 ms and 12 ms, regardless of actual execution duration or system load.
findings.expected: Operational dashboards must display real-time measured latencies computed from recent execution traces (e.g. rolling p50/p95 from decision_traces).
findings.actual: Hardcoded static literals are presented as live telemetry.
findings.impact: Misleading operational observability: Operators cannot detect latency degradation or disconnection from health endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Compute rolling latency metrics from the decision_traces SQLite table and actively probe Razorpay sandbox connectivity.
findings.regression_test_required: Assert that /dashboard/metrics measured latency fluctuates based on actual execution durations.

findings.title: Single-Node SQLite Serialized ACID Guarantee Does Not Scale Across Distributed Instances
findings.observation: Dual-resource locking relies on SQLite's 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION;' via synchronous node:sqlite DatabaseSync. Concurrency control uses local file-locking semantics.
findings.attack_reproduction: Deploy ACG gateway across multiple container instances or worker processes sharing a network disk (NFS/CIFS). Concurrent writes from multiple processes will cause SQLITE_BUSY locking errors or inconsistent lock acquisition.
findings.expected: Distributed deployments require centralized locking (e.g. Redis Redlock) or an enterprise RDBMS with serialized row-level locking (PostgreSQL SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
findings.impact: Architecture limitation: ACG is strictly limited to single-process deployments. Attempting multi-instance horizontal scaling without migrating to PostgreSQL risks database lock starvation or concurrency failures.
findings.evidence: Source code in src/core/reservation.ts:72 ('BEGIN IMMEDIATE TRANSACTION;').
findings.recommendation: Document single-node deployment boundary prominently and wire src/store/postgres_schema.sql with pg connection pooling for cluster deployments.
findings.regression_test_required: Multi-process concurrency test demonstrating SQLITE_BUSY contention under distributed load.

findings.title: Auto-Generated Event ID on Missing Header Bypasses Deduplication
findings.observation: If the incoming webhook omits 'x-razorpay-event-id', router.ts:1171 defaults eventId to 'event_${Date.now()}'.
findings.attack_reproduction: Submit the same webhook payload repeatedly without the 'x-razorpay-event-id' header. Each submission receives a new eventId timestamp, completely bypassing processed_webhook_events deduplication.
findings.expected: Missing 'x-razorpay-event-id' should either reject with HTTP 400 Bad Request or derive a deterministic eventId from sha256(rawBody).
findings.actual: Non-deterministic event ID generation on missing header.
findings.impact: Replay attacks: Missing header allows identical payloads to be processed repeatedly if signature check is satisfied.
findings.evidence: Source code in src/gateway/router.ts:1171 ('const eventId = (request.headers["x-razorpay-event-id"] as string) || `event_${Date.now()}`;').
findings.recommendation: Require 'x-razorpay-event-id' header or derive eventId deterministically via sha256(rawBody).
findings.regression_test_required: Assert that webhook POST without x-razorpay-event-id is rejected or deduplicated deterministically.

findings.title: Audit Ledger Cryptographic Forward-Chain Integrity Verified (Tamper-Evident SHA-256)
findings.observation: Audit records are forward-chained via SHA-256: sha256(auditId|intentId|timestamp|eventType|prevState|newState|detailsJson|prevHash). verifyLedgerIntegrity() validates 307 blocks across ./data/acg_gateway.db (183), ./data/demo_simulation.db (28), and ./data/live_pentest.db (96). Any post-hoc mutation of details, event_type, or hashes is immediately detected.
findings.attack_reproduction: Modify any row in audit_ledger (e.g. UPDATE audit_ledger SET details_json = '{"tampered":true}' WHERE rowid = 2). Running npm run audit:verify immediately terminates with 'Tampered hash at block <audit_id>'.
findings.expected: Immediate detection of any post-hoc state mutation.
findings.actual: Verified tamper-evidence across all 307 historical ledger blocks.
findings.impact: Cryptographic assurance: ACG's audit chain is demonstrably tamper-evident within the storage layer.
findings.evidence: Verification output from scripts/verify_audit.ts and pentest runner test AUDIT-02.
findings.recommendation: Retain term 'TAMPER-EVIDENT SHA-256 HASH CHAIN'. Avoid claiming 'tamper-proof' or legal immutability since local filesystem administrator could recalculate forward hashes.
